summary: @or-sdk/authorizer preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0x`-prefixed identifiers and per-function string-map objects hiding literals such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `unzip`, `powershell`, and the Bun release URL). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...`, extracts it to a temp directory, marks the binary executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` on the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line Bun-compiled JavaScript blob (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with string-array/control-flow-flattening obfuscation (shuffled string-array decoder `WV8StW`, numeric code tables, `_0x` identifiers); its plaintext behavior cannot be recovered without executing the Bun runtime. An OAuth authorizer SDK has no functional need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an obfuscated payload under it during installation. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (executing the real payload only under a smuggled interpreter) bypasses Node-based static analysis of npm packages, and combined with obfuscation of both the loader and the payload, is a supply-chain attack shape. Installing the package causes arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine as a side effect of `npm install`, with concealed behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
